mainTopic: The end of the נובלות discussion, then עולא's limit on the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבנן about which food gets the first ברכה, and the challenge to עולא from the ברייתא of the radish (צנון) and olive (זית).
overview: First the גמרא finishes the earlier discussion of נובלות. It raises a wording problem for the view that they are sun-burned dates, and that problem stays unanswered (קשיא). Then it turns to the משנה about many foods in front of a person. עולא says רבי יהודה and רבנן argue only when the foods share one ברכה; when the ברכות differ, everyone agrees each food gets its own ברכה. A ברייתא about a radish and an olive seems to challenge עולא. The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא as missing words (חסורי מחסרא), so that it fits עולא exactly. Next, רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא argue whether the מחלוקת also applies when the ברכות differ, and רבי ירמיה explains that it would then be about which ברכה comes first. This order is based on the פסוק of the שבעת המינים. רבי חנן reads that פסוק as teaching שיעורין instead, and the גמרא begins listing the measure each species teaches. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A wording problem for the view that נובלות are sun-burned dates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that our משנה says plain נובלות, while the משנה in דמאי says נובלות תמרה. This difference fits one view of what נובלות are, but not the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says these are wind-fallen dates. That is why here (in our משנה) it calls them plain 'נובלות', and there (in דמאי) it calls them 'נובלות תמרה'. They are two different things. But for the one who says these are dates burned by the heat, both משניות should use the same name: either both 'נובלות תמרה', or both plain 'נובלות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier argument between two אמוראים about what נובלות are. It raises a wording problem against the view that they are dates burned by the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נובלות in our משנה and נובלות תמרה in דמאי are two different items, the different names make sense. That fits the view that נובלות תמרה are wind-fallen dates. But if both משניות mean the same sun-burned dates, the משנה should have used one name in both places. The change in wording suggests two different things.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine for… (opens a contrast: one view fits, the other has trouble)
Dates knocked down by the wind
Dates 'cooked' or burned by the heat of the sun
Fallen or withered fruit
This one and that one, meaning both places

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a new topic. It continues the discussion from the previous page about the word נובלות in our משנה. 'Here' means our משנה in ברכות. 'There' means the משנה in מסכת דמאי.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says they are wind-fallen dates,
that is why here it calls them plain 'novelot',
and there it calls them 'temara' (novelot of the date palm),
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה in מסכת דמאי.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says they are dates burned by the heat,
let it teach in both places 'novelot temara',
or in both places plain 'novelot'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier argument (on the previous amud) about the meaning of נובלות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that נובלות are בושלי כמרא (sun-burned dates).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different names in two משניות suggest two different items. Under the sun-burned view they are the same item, so the wording should match.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the wording problem has no answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'קשיא'. This means the problem against the sun-burned view stands, and no answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' does not mean the view is thrown out completely. It means this point remains a real difficulty for that view. The discussion of נובלות ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; an unresolved question

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end of a discussion is weaker than 'תיובתא' (a full refutation). The view is still standing, but it has an open problem.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 1 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The view that נובלות are sun-burned dates is left with an unanswered wording difficulty.

steps.title: עולא limits the dispute to foods with the same ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about many foods. עולא says רבי יהודה and רבנן argue only when the foods share one ברכה. When the ברכות differ, each food gets its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If there were many kinds of food in front of him…'. עולא said: The argument is only when their ברכות are the same. רבי יהודה holds that a food from the seven species comes first. רבנן hold that the food a person likes more comes first. But when their ברכות are not the same, everyone agrees: he makes a ברכה on this one, and then makes another ברכה on that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. עולא then explains exactly when רבי יהודה and רבנן argue about which food gets the ברכה first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the foods share the same ברכה, one ברכה covers all of them. The only question is which food to say it over. רבי יהודה picks the food from שבעת המינים, and רבנן pick the food the person likes most (חביב). When the ברכות differ, one ברכה cannot cover the other food, so each one needs its own ברכה. There is nothing to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
Their ברכות are the same
One of the seven species that ארץ ישראל is praised for
Preferred or beloved by the person
Takes precedence; comes first
Everyone agrees

steps.whyThisMatters: עולא's rule shapes the halacha about the order of ברכות. The order between foods only matters when one ברכה covers them all.

phrases.english: 'If there were many kinds of food before him, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the new topic.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The dispute is when their blessings are the same,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר מִין שִׁבְעָה עָדִיף,
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yehuda holds a type of the seven species takes precedence,
and the Rabbis hold the preferred type takes precedence.
But when their blessings are not the same,
all agree he blesses over this one,
and then blesses again over that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only when the ברכות are the same. When they differ, everyone agrees that each food gets its own ברכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the radish's ברכה covers the olive
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one ברכה on a radish exempts an olive, even though their ברכות are different. This seems to contradict עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If a radish and an olive were in front of him, he blesses on the radish and that exempts the olive!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא with a ברייתא. Here, two foods with different ברכות are covered by one ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A radish is בורא פרי האדמה and an olive is בורא פרי העץ, so their ברכות differ. עולא said that in such a case each food needs its own ברכה. Yet the ברייתא says the radish's ברכה exempts the olive.

keyTerms.meaning: Radish
Olive
Exempts

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If a radish and an olive were before him,

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַצְּנוֹן וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַזַּיִת!
phrases.english: he blesses over the radish and exempts the olive!

steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that foods with different ברכות always need separate ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The radish and the olive have different ברכות, yet one ברכה covers both.

steps.title: The radish is the main food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is a case where the radish is the עיקר. The olive is only a side food.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? When the radish is the main food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a separate rule that a ברכה on the main food (עיקר) covers the side food (טפל), even if their ברכות differ. Here the olive is eaten only to soften the radish's sharp taste. So this case is an exception that falls under עיקר וטפל, not a contradiction of עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a source to a specific case)
The main food

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
When the radish is primary.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (עיקר וטפל).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that foods with different ברכות can share one ברכה in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only happens because the radish is the עיקר and the olive is טפל.

steps.title: Then why would רבי יהודה bless the olive?
steps.stepSummary: If the radish is the main food, רבי יהודה's view in the same ברייתא (bless the olive) is strange. Does he reject the rule of עיקר וטפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: רבי יהודה says he blesses on the olive, because the olive is one of the seven species. Does רבי יהודה not accept what we learned in a משנה: whenever there is a main food with a side food, he blesses on the main food and that exempts the side food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 5 using the second half (סיפא) of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the radish is the עיקר, then by the rule of עיקר וטפל the ברכה must go on the radish. But רבי יהודה says to bless the olive. That would mean he ignores an accepted משנה. So the case cannot be one where the radish is the עיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Look at the end part of the source
Does he not hold of…?
The side, secondary food

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַזַּיִת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says he blesses over the olive,
because the olive is of the seven species.

phrases.aramaic: לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא דִּתְנַן:
phrases.english: Does Rabbi Yehuda not hold that which we learned:
Anything that is primary and has a secondary food with it,

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִיקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה?
phrases.english: he blesses over the primary and exempts the secondary?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא deals with a case where the radish is the עיקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the radish were the עיקר, רבי יהודה would be going against the accepted rule of עיקר וטפל by blessing the olive.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה really does reject עיקר וטפל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible way out: perhaps רבי יהודה indeed does not accept the rule of עיקר וטפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: Yes, it is true that he does not hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: This step is a suggested answer that the גמרא is about to reject. It sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To save the 'radish is עיקר' answer, one could say that רבי יהודה simply disagrees with the משנה of עיקר וטפל. Then his blessing the olive would make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer that will be rejected)
Indeed, that is so

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say: Indeed, he does not hold of it,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested answer: רבי יהודה disagrees with the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה ignoring עיקר וטפל seemed impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps he really does reject that rule.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה accepts עיקר וטפל
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה himself: if the olive is eaten because of the radish, the radish's ברכה covers the olive. So he does accept עיקר וטפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: If the olive comes because of the radish, he blesses on the radish and that exempts the olive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion of step 7 with a ברייתא. רבי יהודה clearly agrees that the main food's ברכה covers the side food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה accepts עיקר וטפל, his ruling to bless the olive must be in a case where the radish is NOT the עיקר. In that case the radish and olive have different ברכות, yet רבי יהודה and רבנן are still arguing about which one to bless. That contradicts עולא, who said there is no dispute when the ברכות differ. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: the order of ברכות is debated only when the foods share one ברכה. The radish-and-olive ברייתא challenges this. The answer 'the radish is עיקר' runs into trouble, because רבי יהודה accepts עיקר וטפל and still says to bless the olive. Step 9 resolves this by reading the ברייתא as missing words (חסורי מחסרא).

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If the olive comes because of the radish,

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַצְּנוֹן וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַזַּיִת.
phrases.english: he blesses over the radish and exempts the olive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 7. This brings back the challenge of step 6 against עולא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יהודה rejects עיקר וטפל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה explicitly applies עיקר וטפל to the radish and the olive.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words, so the dispute is about a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the idea that the radish is the עיקר. It says רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue about a different case, which the ברייתא leaves out, and it rewrites the ברייתא with the missing part added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, we are dealing with a case where the radish is the main food. When רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue, they argue about a different matter. The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it really teaches: If a radish and an olive were in front of him, he says a ברכה on the radish and that covers the olive. When is this true? When the radish is the main food. But if the radish is not the main food, everyone agrees he says a ברכה on this one and then again says a ברכה on that one. And in general, if there are two kinds of food whose ברכות are the same, he may say the ברכה on whichever one he wants. רבי יהודה says: he says the ברכה on the olive, because the olive is one of the שבעת המינים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 8 without giving up its earlier answer. It says the ברייתא has words missing, and it fills them in so that רבי יהודה is arguing about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that רבי יהודה accepts עיקר וטפל, so he cannot be arguing about the radish-as-עיקר case. The rebuilt ברייתא moves his opinion to a new case: two foods whose ברכות are the same (שני מינין בעלמא שברכותיהן שוות), where the only question is which one to bless. This now fits עולא exactly: when the ברכות differ (radish not עיקר), everyone agrees on two ברכות, and the dispute is only when the ברכות are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. It signals that the גמרא is keeping its earlier position.
The text is missing words. Some words have to be added to the ברייתא.
And this is what it really teaches. It introduces the corrected text.
In what case are these words said? It limits a rule to a specific situation.
Whose ברכות are the same (for example, both בורא פרי העץ).
One of the שבעת המינים, the seven special fruits and grains of ארץ ישראל.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה is still arguing about the radish and olive when the radish is the עיקר. In the corrected ברייתא, everyone agrees about that case. רבי יהודה's opinion now belongs only to the new case of two foods with the same ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known tool of the גמרא: fixing a ברייתא by saying words are missing. It lets the גמרא keep both its answer about עולא and the fact that רבי יהודה accepts עיקר וטפל.

phrases.english: Actually, we are dealing with a case where the radish is the main food,
and when Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis disagree,
they disagree about a different matter,
and the text is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
phrases.notes: From here on is the ברייתא with the missing words filled back in.

phrases.english: If a radish and an olive were in front of him,

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַצְּנוֹן וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַזַּיִת.
phrases.english: he blesses on the radish and exempts the olive.
When does this apply? When the radish is the main food,
but if the radish is not the main food,
everyone agrees he blesses on this one
and then again blesses on that one.
And in general, two kinds of food whose blessings are the same:
he blesses on whichever of them he wants.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַזַּיִת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: he blesses on the olive,
because the olive is one of the seven species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 8 rejected the idea that רבי יהודה denies עיקר וטפל, this step brings back Step 5's answer. It does so by rebuilding the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: rewriting the ברייתא so that the dispute is about a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה argues even when the radish is the עיקר, which would mean he rejects עיקר וטפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone accepts עיקר וטפל. רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue only about two foods with the same ברכה: which one to choose.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree on the scope of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue about where רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree. One says only when the ברכות are the same. The other says even when the ברכות are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree about this. One says: the dispute is only when the ברכות are the same. רבי יהודה holds that one of the שבעת המינים comes first, and the רבנן hold that the food the person likes more comes first. But when the ברכות are not the same, everyone agrees he says a ברכה on this one and then says a ברכה on that one. The other says: even when the ברכות are not the same, there is also a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how far the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן reaches. One limits it to foods with the same ברכה. The other says it applies even to foods with different ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion explains the reasoning of each side. רבי יהודה ranks a food by its importance as one of the שבעת המינים (מין שבעה עדיף). The רבנן rank it by how much the person likes it (מין חביב עדיף). The second opinion stretches the dispute to foods with different ברכות. Steps 11 and 12 explain what they would argue about there.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about it.
One of the שבעת המינים gets priority.
The food the person likes more gets priority.
Everyone agrees.

steps.confusionAlert: מין חביב means the food that this particular person likes more. It does not mean a food that is important in general.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha disagree about this.
One said: the dispute is when their blessings are the same,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר מִין שִׁבְעָה עָדִיף,
phrases.english: for Rabbi Yehuda holds one of the seven species takes priority,
and the Rabbis hold the preferred food takes priority.
But when their blessings are not the same,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מְבָרֵךְ עַל זֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּמְבָרֵךְ עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: everyone agrees he blesses on this one and then again blesses on that one.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אַף בְּשֶׁאֵין בִּרְכוֹתֵיהֶן שָׁווֹת
phrases.english: And one said: even when their blessings are not the same
there is also a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge to עולא is resolved, the גמרא brings a parallel אמורא dispute about the scope of the משנה's מחלוקת. The first view is identical to עולא's statement in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: the dispute is only when the ברכות are the same (מין שבעה versus מין חביב). Second view: the dispute exists even when the ברכות are different.

steps.title: What could they argue about if two blessings are needed anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The first view makes sense. But according to the second view, if the ברכות are different you must say two ברכות no matter what, so what is left to argue about?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says the dispute is when the ברכות are the same. But according to the one who says they argue even when the ברכות are not the same, what are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second opinion. If each food needs its own ברכה, there seems to be nothing to argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ברכות are the same, it is clear what the argument is: which food to choose so that one ברכה covers both. When the ברכות are different, both foods get a ברכה anyway. So the second opinion seems to leave the dispute with no content.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted. It sets up a contrast with a view that is harder to explain.
Fine, it works well.
About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
the dispute is when their blessings are the same, it works well,
but according to the one who says
they disagree when their blessings are not the same,
about what do they disagree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּשֶׁבִּרְכוֹתֵיהֶן שָׁווֹת מַחֲלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the second opinion from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the dispute applies even when the ברכות are not the same.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Foods with different ברכות always need two ברכות, so there is no practical question left to argue about.

steps.title: They argue about which blessing comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that the argument is about order: which food gets its ברכה first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: they argue about which one to say first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question from Step 11. Even when both foods get a ברכה, there is still a question of which ברכה is said first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute does not have to be about how many ברכות to say. It can also be about their order. So רבי יהודה would say the food from the שבעת המינים goes first, and the רבנן would say the food the person likes more goes first, even when two ברכות are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To put first: which ברכה is said first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: regarding which comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the dispute is about: the order of the ברכות, not their number.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With different ברכות there seemed to be nothing to argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about which ברכה comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: When foods have the same ברכה, the question is which food to choose for the one ברכה. When they have different ברכות, according to one view, the question is which ברכה to say first.

steps.title: Foods listed earlier in the verse get their blessing first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source showing that ברכות do have an order: foods listed earlier in the פסוק of the שבעת המינים come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף, and some say רבי יצחק, said: whatever comes first in this פסוק comes first for the ברכה. As it says: "A land of wheat and barley, and vine and fig and pomegranate, a land of olive oil and honey."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי ירמיה's answer with a known teaching. Foods have an order of importance for ברכות, and it follows the order of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that order really matters for ברכות, which is what makes רבי ירמיה's answer work. The teaching gives a clear ranking: foods mentioned earlier in the פסוק get their ברכה first. This is the basis for רבי יהודה's view that the שבעת המינים have priority.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes first for the ברכה.
As it is said (introducing a פסוק).

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the source for the halachic order of ברכות among the שבעת המינים.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: As Rav Yosef said, and some say Rabbi Yitzchak:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמּוּקְדָּם בְּפָסוּק זֶה, מוּקְדָּם לִבְרָכָה,
phrases.english: whatever comes first in this verse comes first for the blessing,
as it is said: "A land of wheat and barley,
and vine and fig and pomegranate,
a land of olive oil and honey." (Deuteronomy 8:8)

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives a source supporting רבי ירמיה's answer that ברכות have an order of priority.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a set order for saying ברכות on different foods.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רב יוסף (or רבי יצחק), based on דברים 8:8.

steps.title: This view argues with רבי חנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that using the פסוק to set the order of ברכות disagrees with רבי חנן, who says the whole פסוק is about measurements.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רבי חנן. For רבי חנן said: the entire פסוק was said to teach measurements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the idea from the last step, that the פסוק sets the order of ברכות, is not accepted by everyone. רבי חנן reads the same פסוק in a totally different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 used the order of the פסוק of the שבעת המינים to decide which ברכה comes first. רבי חנן says the purpose of the whole פסוק is to teach halachic measurements (שיעורין). So by his reading, the פסוק is not a source for ordering ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees (with someone else's view)
Halachic measurements: set amounts of size or time
A verse; here, the פסוק listing the שבעת המינים (דברים 8:8)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנן is not arguing about which ברכה to make. He is only saying that this פסוק was written for a different purpose, which is teaching measurements.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one פסוק can be read for very different purposes. It also opens the long list of measurements that follows.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Chanan.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the view that the פסוק sets the order of ברכות.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Chanan said:
The entire verse was stated for measurements.
phrases.notes: Each species in the פסוק teaches a halachic amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that the source used in step 13 is read differently by רבי חנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנן, the פסוק of the שבעת המינים teaches שיעורין, not the order of ברכות.

steps.title: Wheat teaches the time measure in a house with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The measure of time 'enough to eat half a loaf' is based on wheat bread, so wheat in the פסוק teaches a שיעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wheat': as we learned in a משנה. One who enters a house with צרעת while carrying his clothes on his shoulders, with his sandals and rings in his hands, becomes טמא right away, and so do the items. If he was wearing his clothes, with his sandals on his feet and his rings on his fingers, he becomes טמא right away, but the items stay טהור until he stays long enough to eat a פרס. This means wheat bread, not barley bread, eaten while reclining and with a relish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the פסוק one fruit at a time. It shows that 'wheat' is the basis for a measure of time in the laws of a בית המנוגע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Items he is carrying become טמא right away. Items he is wearing only become טמא if he stays as long as it takes to eat a פרס, which is half a loaf. That length of time is measured by the fastest way of eating: wheat bread (not barley), eaten reclining, with a relish. So wheat sets the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A house struck with צרעת (a type of spiritual 'leprosy' affecting houses)
Half a loaf; the time it takes to eat it is a set measure
A relish or side dish eaten with bread
Reclining, the relaxed way of eating

steps.confusionAlert: The person himself becomes טמא right away in both cases. The difference between carrying and wearing only matters for his clothes and items.

phrases.english: 'Wheat': as we learned in a mishna:
One who enters a house afflicted with tzaraas,
with his clothes on his shoulders,
and his sandals and rings in his hands,
he and they are impure immediately.
If he was wearing his clothes,
and his sandals on his feet, and his rings on his fingers,
he is impure immediately,
but they remain pure until he stays
long enough to eat half a loaf.
Wheat bread and not barley bread,
phrases.notes: Wheat bread is eaten faster, and this is where 'wheat' comes in.

phrases.english: reclining and eating it with a relish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining רבי חנן's claim with the first species.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנן's claim that חטה in the פסוק teaches a שיעור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about entering a בית המנוגע (נגעים 13:9)

steps.title: Barley teaches the size of a bone that makes things טמא
steps.stepSummary: A bone of a dead body the size of a barley grain makes things טמא by touching and carrying, but not through אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Barley': as we learned in a משנה. A bone the size of a barley grain makes things טמא by touching and by carrying, but it does not make things טמא through אהל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next species, barley. It shows that barley sets the minimum size of a bone from a מת that can spread טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bone as small as a barley grain is enough to make someone טמא if he touches it or carries it. It is not enough to make everything under the same roof טמא, which is called טומאת אהל. The barley grain is the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A bone (of a dead body) the size of a barley grain
Touching
Carrying or lifting
Being under the same roof as a מת, which spreads טומאה

phrases.english: 'Barley': as we learned in a mishna:
A bone the size of a barley grain
imparts impurity through contact and carrying,
but does not impart impurity through a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the second species.
steps.raayaObject: שעורה in the פסוק teaches a שיעור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a bone the size of a barley grain (אהלות 2:3)

steps.title: Vine and fig teach the נזיר's amount and the שבת carrying amount
steps.stepSummary: The vine teaches a רביעית of wine for a נזיר. The fig teaches that carrying a גרוגרת-sized amount of food on שבת makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Vine': a רביעית of wine for a נזיר. 'Fig': the size of a dried fig, for carrying out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quickly gives two more measurements: one from the vine and one from the fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נזיר, the measure of wine is a רביעית, which is a quarter לוג. For carrying food from one רשות to another on שבת, the minimum amount is the size of a גרוגרת, a dried fig. Each fruit in the פסוק supplies a measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter לוג, a measure of liquid
A person who vowed not to drink wine, among other things
A dried fig; the minimum food amount for liability when carrying on שבת
Carrying out from one domain to another on שבת

phrases.english: 'Vine': the amount of a quarter log of wine for a Nazirite.
'Fig': the size of a dried fig
for carrying out on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the third and fourth species.
steps.raayaObject: גפן and תאנה in the פסוק teach שיעורין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The known measures of a נזיר's wine and of carrying on שבת

steps.title: Pomegranate begins: household utensils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show the measure taught by the pomegranate. It quotes the start of a משנה about household utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Pomegranate': as we learned in a משנה: all utensils of ordinary homeowners...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next measure, the one from the pomegranate. It starts quoting a משנה about household utensils, and the rest continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, only the opening words of the משנה appear. The משנה will explain how big a hole must be in a homeowner's utensil before it stops being a כלי and becomes טהור. The size of a pomegranate will turn out to be that measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Pomegranate
Utensils of ordinary homeowners, as opposed to craftsmen's tools

steps.confusionAlert: This step is cut off in the middle of the משנה. The actual measure comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: 'Pomegranate': as we learned in a mishna:
All utensils of homeowners
phrases.notes: The משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the fifth species in רבי חנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: רמון in the פסוק teaches a שיעור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about homeowners' utensils (כלים 17:1), continued on the next amud
